summary: The root names a thing whole and complete. כֹּל is “all, the whole, every”; כָּלִיל is “entire”, an offering given wholly to the altar, and beauty brought to perfection; the verb is to complete or perfect, in Hebrew of Tyre’s beauty and in Ezra’s Aramaic of finishing the temple and the walls. כַּלָּה names the bride and the daughter-in-law; the Peshitta has the crown and crowning in the same root. Cognates attest every one of these families, ‘all’ and ‘complete’ across the whole Semitic area, the bride in Akkadian, Ugaritic and Aramaic, and the crown, veil and wedding together in Akkadian, Aramaic and Ge’ez. Scripture joins the bride to the ‘complete’ sense through her array: “all of you is beautiful, and there is no blemish in you” is followed at once by “bride” (Sng 4:7–8), and Jerusalem, taken in covenant, clothed, adorned and crowned, is made perfect (כָּלִיל) in beauty (Ezk 16:8–14). The bride is the one made complete in her adornment, the crown its finishing piece, beside מִכְלוֹל “full array” and מַכְלֻל “finery”.

senses.definition: An entire quantity or set, whose bounds are given by the following noun or the context.

evidence.note: God sees all that he has made.
All the congregation of the sons of Israel comes to the wilderness of Sin.
Love Yahweh with all your heart, soul and might; quoted in Mat 22:37.

senses.definition: Each member of a class; under a negative, not any member.

evidence.note: From every tree of the garden you may eat.
You shall not do any work.

senses.definition: Standing alone, often with the article (הַכֹּל): everything that exists or is in view.

evidence.note: “I am Yahweh, who makes all things (עֹשֶׂה כֹּל)”, stretching out the heavens alone.
His kingdom rules over all.
He has made everything beautiful in its time.

senses.definition: The woman entering marriage, set beside the bridegroom, and the image for Yahweh’s people adorned and rejoiced over.

evidence.note: “The voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.”
As the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your God rejoices over you.
A bride adorns herself with her jewels.
Zion binds on her returning children as a bride does her ornaments.
Straight after “all of you is beautiful, my love, and there is no blemish in you” (4:7), he calls her כַּלָּה.
Can a bride forget her attire?

senses.definition: The wife of someone’s son.

evidence.note: “Your daughter-in-law … she is your son’s wife.”
Sarai is Terah’s daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram.
Daughter-in-law against mother-in-law; quoted in Mat 10:35.

words.summary: The woman in a marriage, or the wife of one’s son: the same two senses as Akkadian kallātu and Aramaic כַּלְּתָא, and Ugaritic klt “bride”. These languages have the word as a plain noun, so they do not show it was formed from “complete”. What they do show is a cluster around the bride in the same consonants: Akkadian kullulu “veiled” of a bride and “to crown”, Aramaic כְּלַל “crown” and “be married”, Ge’ez “crowning” for a wedding, and perhaps Sabaic hkll “give in marriage”. Scripture supplies the tie to the root’s ‘complete’ sense: the Song calls her wholly beautiful and without blemish and then names her bride (Sng 4:7–8), and Ezekiel’s Jerusalem, married, adorned and crowned, is כָּלִיל in beauty (Ezk 16:8–14). The bride is the one brought to completeness in her array, and the daughter-in-law is that same bride as the son’s household receives her.

senses.definition: The whole of a thing, or made entirely of one material.

evidence.note: The robe is entirely of blue.
A cloth wholly of blue is spread over the ark.
The whole of the city goes up in smoke to the heavens.

senses.definition: As an adverb: completely, leaving nothing.

evidence.note: The idols shall utterly pass away.
The city and all its spoil burnt כָּלִיל to Yahweh: wholly, and as a whole offering.

senses.definition: An offering given wholly to the altar, of which nothing is eaten.

evidence.note: Every priest’s grain offering is כָּלִיל: it shall not be eaten.
Wholly made to smoke to Yahweh.
Samuel offers a lamb as a whole burnt offering.
Burnt offering and whole offering, beside “sacrifices of righteousness”.

senses.definition: Brought to completeness in a quality; in the construct כְּלִיל(ַת) יֹפִי “perfect of beauty”, said of Jerusalem and of Tyre.

evidence.note: Jerusalem’s beauty is perfect through the splendour Yahweh put on her, after he clothed and adorned her and set a crown on her head (16:8–13).
“The perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth.”
Tyre says, “I am perfect of beauty.”

senses.definition: Bring something to its full state; both occurrences are of builders and defenders completing Tyre’s beauty, the city pictured as a ship.

evidence.note: Your builders perfected your beauty.
Their shields hung on your walls all around perfected your beauty.

senses.definition: Complete and splendid equipment or dress, in which warriors are clothed.

evidence.note: Assyrian governors and warriors clothed in מִכְלוֹל, riding horses.
Gog’s horsemen, all clothed in מִכְלוֹל, with shield, buckler and sword.

words.summary: “Clothed in completeness”: both occurrences describe soldiers fully and splendidly arrayed. The noun is formed like מִכְלָל “perfection”; Akkadian šuklultu “completeness” of decoration and Aramaic שַׁכְלֵל “finish, decorate” show the same sense of finished adornment. The exact garment or gear is not fixed by two uses.

senses.definition: Perfected or splendid goods in Tyre’s trade, listed first before fabrics of blue, embroidery and carpets; attested only here, in the plural.

evidence.note: Merchants trading in מַכְלֻלִים, wrappings of blue and embroidered work, and carpets.

words.summary: A passive form, “things made perfect”: in one verse, among textiles, so probably fine garments or finished wares. Its sense rests on the root and on this one context.

senses.definition: The complete or perfect expression of a quality; in its single occurrence, Zion’s beauty.

evidence.note: Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth.
The same phrase with כְּלִילַת יֹפִי, of Jerusalem.

senses.definition: The time or state of being a bride, in the image of Israel’s early devotion to Yahweh.

evidence.note: The love of your כְּלוּלֹת is parallel to the devotion of your youth, following Yahweh in the wilderness.

words.summary: Attested only in a plural abstract for Israel’s bridal time. It is formed from the bride-word; whether betrothal or the wedding itself is meant is not fixed by this verse alone.

senses.definition: A whole set, or each member of it.

evidence.note: The king is made ruler over them all.
The kingdom devours the whole earth.

senses.definition: Bring construction to completion: the temple, its structure, or a city’s walls.

evidence.note: A great king of Israel built the house and completed it.
They built and completed it by the decree of the God of Israel.
They are finishing the walls (שַׁכְלִילוּ).
Who gave you a decree to build this house and to complete this structure?

senses.definition: Of walls whose building is finished.

evidence.note: If the city is rebuilt and its walls completed.

words.summary: Like Akkadian šuklulu and Targumic שַׁכְלֵל, a Š-stem of the root: “make complete”. Sabaic kll uses the same pairing, “he built and completed”, as Ezra 5:11 does.

senses.definition: The whole of something or every member of a stated class.

evidence.note: All the generations are counted in three groups.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down.

senses.definition: The woman joined to a bridegroom, and the holy city prepared as the Lamb’s bride.

evidence.note: The one who has the bride is the bridegroom.
“The bride, the wife of the Lamb.”
The holy city prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.

senses.definition: A son’s wife, set in relation to her mother-in-law.

evidence.note: Daughter-in-law and mother-in-law are set against one another, from Mic 7:6.

senses.definition: A head-wreath, including the crown of thorns.

evidence.note: They weave thorns into a crown and place it on his head.

senses.definition: A crown promised or awarded, or a person spoken of as someone’s crown.

evidence.note: Athletes compete for a perishable crown; believers for an imperishable one.
The one who endures testing receives the crown of life.

words.summary: A circlet or wreath worn on the head, and figuratively a reward or honor. Akkadian kullulu “to crown” (of a king, and of a gate “crowned” with battlements) and Aramaic כְּלִיל “wreath, crown” are the same word-family; Akkadian kilīlu “wreath”, which some derive the Aramaic noun from, also means battlement. Crowning a wall is finishing it. In scripture the crown is the last piece of the bride’s array: Yahweh sets a crown on Jerusalem’s head, and her beauty is then perfect (כָּלִיל, Ezk 16:12–14).

senses.definition: Receive the athlete’s crown; this verb occurs only here in the Peshitta.

evidence.note: An athlete is not crowned unless he competes lawfully.

cognates.note: The noun’s constructions express a whole or any member; the adjective kulliyy means total or universal.

evidence.note: "totality, all of ..." OAkk, Bab.(lit.); absol. "whole (world)"; before subst., pron. suff. "all of ...".
"all, totality": the commoner Akkadian word for “all”.

cognates.note: Akkadian has both kullatu and kalû for the whole and for “all of”.

evidence.note: "The expression kl /kull-/ is basically a noun meaning “wholeness.” ... It occurs before the singular (English “every”): kl ġr 1.6:II:15–16 “every mountain” ... klhm 1.14:II:42 “all of them.”"
"kl /kull-/ “every, all”; klh, klhm ... (cf. H. kōl, kål-, kull-, Aram. kål-, kŏllā, Arab. kull-)".

cognates.note: Ugaritic, with the Hebrew constructions: before a singular “every”, with suffixes “all of it, all of them”.

evidence.note: "[Heb. kol] pron. 1. ALL, EVERY, EACH (ONE) ... 2. ANYONE ... 3. EVERYTHING ... adj. 1. ALL", KAI 26 A I 18/19 kl hmlkm, "all the kings who preceded me"; "2. EVERY, ANY", KAI 69.20 kl khn, "any priest".
Line 4 השעני מכל השלכן ... הראני בכל שנאי; line 11 ואהרג את כל העמ; line 16 ואהרג כלה; line 24 ואמר לכל העמ; line 28 כי כל דיבן משמעת.
"he had saved me from all the assailants (?)"; "slew all of it, 7000 men"; "200 men, all the head-men thereof"; "I said to all the people"; "all Daiḇôn was loyal".

cognates.note: Moabite, the Mesha stele, with the Hebrew uses: before a noun, and with a suffix (כלה “all of it”).

cognates.gloss: all, every; the whole; everything; entirety

evidence.locator: p. 247, KLL, n¹ kl, n² klm, n⁴ klyt
evidence.note: kl "ALL, EVERY; ALL OF, THE WHOLE (OF) [Ar kull id.]", J550/1 "the whole fill of the wall and all the niches"; klm "EVERYTHING, ANYTHING, ALL", MuBilinguis/3 "the Lord of heaven and earth, who created everything"; klyt "ENTIRETY [Ar kulliyat id.]".

cognates.note: Sabaic, filed with the verb “bring to completion” under one root KLL. “Who created everything” matches Isa 44:24 עֹשֶׂה כֹּל.

evidence.locator: cols. 814–815, I. ከለለ, ኵል and ኵሉ
evidence.note: "I. ከለለ rad. inus., cui significatus absolvendi, perficiendi inerat"; ኵል "proprie: universitas"; ኵሉ "A) Refertur ad res multas ... omnis ... B) Refertur ad rem unam, continuam ... totus".

cognates.note: Ge’ez. Dillmann sets ‘all’ under an unused verbal root whose sense he gives as “finishing, perfecting”: the same pairing of ‘all’ with ‘complete’ as Hebrew.

evidence.note: "all, every one; any", Targ. O. Gen. XVI, 12; Targ. Ex. XX, 9.

cognates.note: The Targums’ Aramaic, as in Daniel and Ezra.

cognates.gloss: (Š of kll) complete, make or do completely, perform perfectly; (adj.) complete, perfect, entire

evidence.note: Root kll. Š "to complete, make/do completely"; "create perfectly" humans, form, statue; house, city etc.; "perform perfectly" cult; Št of house "be completed".
"complete, perfect" of things; temples, cult; "entire, uncastrated" of sacrificial animals.
"completion; completeness" jB of decor; "form" of human body.

cognates.note: The Š-stem of the root, like Ezra’s שַׁכְלֵל. It is used of finishing a house or city (Ezra’s temple and walls), of perfect form and decoration (Tyre’s and Zion’s beauty), and of sacrificial animals offered entire (כָּלִיל, the whole offering).

cognates.gloss: bring to completion; (n.) completion, payment in full

evidence.note: "BRING TO COMPLETION [Cf Aram šaklil, Akk šuklulu “finish,” PBH kālīl “entire.”]", J842/3 bny wkl fnwthw "he built and completed his canal"; R3902b#130/2 bnyy wkll ṭlf ḥrt "they built and completed the embankment of the aqueduct".
"COMPLETION > PAYMENT IN FULL", C548/13–4.

cognates.note: Sabaic building inscriptions pair “built and completed” exactly as Ezra 5:11 and 6:14 do.

evidence.note: "to finish, decorate. Targ. Y. Ex. XXXI, 17. Targ. Ez. XXVII, 4; 11 ... Part. pass. מְשַׁכְלַל ... perfect. Ib. 3. Ib. XXVIII, 12"; Ithpa. "to be finished, decorated. Targ. O. Gen. II, 1".

cognates.note: The Targums use this verb for the heavens and earth “finished” (Gen 2:1) and to render Ezekiel’s כָּלַל and כְּלִיל יֹפִי (27:3, 4, 11; 28:12): finishing and adorning are one act in it.

evidence.note: "kll /kalīl-/ (?) “whole” 1.115:10 = 82.5 (cf. H. kəlīl constr. Judg 20:40)".
Ritual rubric š lilbt šlmm kll ylḥm bh: "/kalīlu/ “whole” (cf. H. kālīl, esp. Jdg 20:40) or kl lylḥm (?) /kullu lā yilḥamū/ (?) “all will/must not eat”; or cf. H. Lev 6:15–16 (?)".

cognates.note: In a sacrificial rubric, beside a peace offering, with “they shall (not) eat of it”: Segert compares Lev 6:15–16, where the כָּלִיל is not eaten.

evidence.note: "[Heb. kalīl] adj. ENTIRE, WHOLE", KAI 69.3 (Pu) b'lp kll 'm ṣwʿt 'm šlm kll, "For an entire ox, whether cut in pieces or entirely intact, the priests shall receive ten 10 silver"; "adv. ENTIRELY, COMPLETELY", CIS i 88.2/3 "presented and erected this statue and completely restored it".

cognates.note: Punic, in the Marseilles sacrificial tariff: the animal offered entire, as with the כָּלִיל.

evidence.note: "daughter-in-law, bride" of human, deities; OB ana kallāt ū mārat "to be daughter-in-law and daughter"; also "young woman, bride" in gener.

cognates.note: The same two senses as כַּלָּה.

evidence.note: "klt /kallat-/ “bride” (H. kallā, Syr. kalltā, Akkad. kallātu)".
"bride; daughter-in-law. Targ. Is. LXI, 10 ... Targ. Gen. XI, 31"; Gitt. 57ᵃ "when they led forth bride and groom in procession".

"GIVE IN MARRIAGE (?) [Cf Ug klt “bride, marriageable girl,” Heb kallāh “bride, daughter-in-law,” Akk kallatu id.]", Ir24 "may (the god) succeed in allowing him to bring, offer and give in marriage this woman".

cognates.note: One occurrence, its sense marked uncertain by the dictionary. If right, the bride-word and “complete” stand under one Sabaic root KLL.

cognates.gloss: (D of kll) veil, crown; (adj.) veiled, of a bride

evidence.note: Root kll. D "to veil, crown" O/jB, M/NA face, lips, in distress; MA "crown" king; jB stat. of gate "is crowned" with crenellations.
"veiled, covered" M/jB of bride.

cognates.note: Crowning a king and veiling a bride are one Akkadian verb of the root, and a gate is “crowned” with its battlements, the course that finishes a wall. This is the closest cognate link between the crown, the bride and the root’s other senses.

cognates.gloss: surround, crown; be crowned, be married; (n.) wreath, crown

evidence.note: "to surround, crown. Targ. Cant. III, 11"; Pa. "to surround, crown. Targ. Ps. V, 13"; "to prepare a bridal room"; Ithpe. "to be crowned, to adorn one’s self"; "to be led into the bridal room, be married".
"circle, wreath, crown. Targ. Y. II, Ex. XXV, 11. Targ. Num. VI, 7 (h. text נֵזֶר) ... Gitt. 7ᵃ כ׳ לברתיה a bridal wreath for his daughter".

cognates.note: The Targum of Song 3:11 uses it for the crown with which his mother crowned the king “on the day of his wedding”; later Aramaic uses the same verb for being married.

cognates.gloss: crown; surround like a crown; (ተክሊል) crowning of bride and groom, wedding

evidence.locator: cols. 816–817, II. ከለለ; ክሉል; አክሊል; ተክሊል
evidence.note: "1) coronare ... 2) coronae instar cingere, circumdari, circumstare"; ክሉል "coronatus"; አክሊል "corona, diadema"; ተክሊል "coronatio (sponsi et sponsae ...) i. e. nuptiae et consecratio nuptialis".
"crown, diadem, tiara, mitre"; "Borrowed from Arabic إِكْلِيل (ʔiklīl)."

cognates.note: Dillmann files the crown root apart from “all” (I. ከለለ). Its wedding sense comes from the church’s crowning of bride and groom, and Wiktionary takes አክሊል as a loan from Arabic, which itself has the crown-noun from Aramaic; so it may be a borrowed word, not an inherited one.

evidence.note: "wreath" OAkk, Bab., NA [GILIM]; no root given.
Meanings: crown, head ornament, wreath, mural crown, battlement, parapet.
Glosses include "crown, wreath" and "finishing, completion (of a building)"; derives it through Aramaic from Akkadian kilīlu.

cognates.note: Written with a Sumerian sign, so it may be a loan into Akkadian; Wiktionary takes the Aramaic and Syriac crown-noun from it. Its use for a wall’s battlements matches kullulu.

cognates.gloss: adorn with gems or jewels; wreathe, crown

evidence.note: كَلَّلَ "He adorned a thing with gems or jewels"; مُكَلَّلٌ "Adorned with gems or jewels".
كلل "to adorn, to wreath", "to crown", "to perform a marriage ceremony, to marry"; إكليل "crown, garland, wreath", "From Aramaic כְלִילָא".

cognates.note: Arabic’s ordinary verb كَلَّ means to tire or be blunt, unrelated in sense; the adorning and crowning verb sits beside إكليل, which Wiktionary takes from Aramaic, so it may be borrowed.

doctrine.statement: Israel is to love Yahweh with all (בְּכָל) the heart, all the soul and all the strength (Deu 6:5), and to seek him with all the heart, which he answers by being found (Deu 4:29; Jer 29:13). He promises to circumcise the heart so that it can love him with all of it (Deu 30:6). Jesus names this the first and great commandment (Mat 22:37–38; Mrk 12:29–30). What is asked is not part of a person but the whole.

Yahweh remembers Israel’s first devotion as “the love of your bridal days”, following him in the wilderness (Jer 2:2). He takes Jerusalem in covenant, clothes and adorns her and sets a crown on her head, and her beauty is perfect (כָּלִיל) through his splendour (Ezk 16:8–14). Restored Zion is rejoiced over by her God as a bridegroom rejoices over the bride (Isa 62:5), clothed with salvation as a bride adorned (Isa 61:10). John names Jesus the bridegroom to whom the bride belongs (Jhn 3:29), and the holy city, new Jerusalem, comes down prepared as a bride adorned for her husband, the bride, the Lamb’s wife (Rev 21:2, 9).

note: Cognates checked on the page: Segert pp. 88, 132, 189; Krahmalkov pp. 226, 229 (Krahmalkov has no klt “bride”); Biella pp. 246–247; Dillmann cols. 814–817 (page images n430, n431); eBL entries as cited; Compston’s Moabite text. Not consulted: Leslau CDG (Ge’ez kʷəll, kallala), CAD K/Š (kalālu, kilīlu, kullulu, šuklulu), Fisher 1969 (OCR poor here; its pp. ~108–109 compare Ug kl/klat with Ethiopic and mention Tigre/Amharic kallala “protect, surround”), Payne Smith/Brockelmann for Syriac ܟܠܝܠܐ “completion (of a building)” — worth confirming, since it would join crown and completion inside Syriac. Open questions: (1) is the bride-word from the root (Sabaic hkll “give in marriage (?)” under KLL; Akkadian kullulu “veiled” of a bride and “crown”) or a separate primary noun that only shares the letters? (2) is the crown-family inherited (Akkadian kullulu, root kll per eBL) or a wandering loan from kilīlu (Wiktionary’s view; Ge’ez and Arabic crown words are then loans)? A crown on a wall is its finishing course (kullulu of a gate, kilīlu “battlement”), which may be how crown joins “complete”. (3) Ugaritic kll in KTU 1.115:10 may be read kl l- “all … not”; Segert gives both. Ezra 4:12 שַׁכְלִילוּ is not counted under xk.ad.aa in the database (ketiv/qere spelling); it is cited by hand. כְּלָל is a person’s name, left for its own entry; the remaining unassigned BDB rows are redirects. xk.ad.ab and k.bn.ab overlap on Hebrew spellings, so their support counts cannot be read as separate language totals. The brief for כלל omits the Aramaic quantifier because it is filed under כל; that word is included here. Doctrine items added 2026-11-09 for review.
